title: Customer Notification & Consent Template — Time-Bound Support Access (Private Deployments)
author: Camila Reyes
content:
# Purpose
This page provides the required **customer communication** steps and templates when Redwood requests **time-bound support access** (JIT / break-glass) to a customer’s **Private deployment** for troubleshooting.

# When to use
Use this whenever Redwood engineers need any of the following in a Private deployment:
- Administrative console access
- Direct node/pod access
- Network tunnel/VPN/WireGuard support tunnel
- Teleport/SSM session access

# Required checklist (CS owner)
Before access is enabled, ensure the support ticket includes:
- Clear reason for access (what we’re diagnosing)
- Expected scope (systems/hosts)
- Expected duration (default 2 hours; max 4 hours per approval cycle)
- Access method (Teleport / WireGuard support tunnel / AWS SSM)
- Names of Redwood personnel who will access
- Confirmation of customer consent (“Approved”)

# Consent language (paste into ticket or email)
**Template (ticket comment):**
Customer consent for time-bound support access (Private deployment):
- Customer approver: <name, title>
- Approved access method: <Teleport / support tunnel / SSM>
- Scope: <targets/ports/namespaces>
- Duration: <start time> to <end time>
- Purpose: <brief>

# Customer email template
Subject: Request for time-bound support access to your Private deployment

Hi <Customer Name>,

To troubleshoot <issue>, we request **time-bound support access** to your **Private deployment**. We will use least-privilege access and will revoke access immediately after the work is complete.

Proposed details:
- Purpose: <what we will investigate>
- Access method: <Teleport / WireGuard support tunnel / AWS SSM>
- Scope: <systems/hosts/services>
- Duration: <2 hours> (max <4 hours> without re-approval)
- Redwood participants: <names>
- Logging: session/audit logs will be captured per our policy

Please reply to approve, or let us know constraints you need (narrower scope, specific hours, customer-only actions, etc.).

Thanks,
<CS Owner>

# During access: customer updates
- For Sev-1: provide an update at least every 30–60 minutes while access is active
- For non-Sev incidents: update when access begins and when access ends

# After access ends: required follow-up
Within 1 business day, post to the ticket and (if requested) email the customer:
- Start/end time
- Who accessed
- What was checked/changed
- Confirmation that access was revoked
- Any recommended next steps

# Notes on terminology (for search/retrieval)
This process may be referenced as: **JIT access**, **time-bound access**, **temporary admin access**, **break-glass access**, or **support access tunnel** for **Private deployments**.
